readings.title: Prisoners’ Dreams Interpreted
readings.text: [Genesis 40:1] And it came to be after these matters that the butler and the baker of the sovereign of Mitsrayim sinned against their master, the sovereign of Mitsrayim. [2] And Pharaoh was wroth with his two officers, the chief butler and the chief baker. [3] So he put them in confinement in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison, the place where Yosĕph was confined. [4] And the captain of the guard appointed Yosĕph to be with them, and he attended them. And they were in confinement for some time. [5] And the butler and the baker of the sovereign of Mitsrayim, who were confined in the prison, both dreamed a dream in one night, each one’s dream with its own interpretation. [6] And Yosĕph came in to them in the morning and looked at them, and saw that they were sad. [7] So he asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in confinement in his master’s house, saying, “Why are your faces so sad today?” [8] And they said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.” And Yosĕph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to <dn>Elohim</dn>? Please relate them to me.” [9] And the chief butler related his dream to Yosĕph, and said to him, “See, in my dream a vine was before me, [10] and on the vine were three branches. And it was as though it budded, its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes. [11] “And Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand. So I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.” [12] And Yosĕph said to him, “This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days. [13] “Yet within three days Pharaoh shall lift up your head and restore you to your place, and you shall put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand according to the former ruling, when you were his butler. [14] “But remember me when it is well with you, and please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and take me out of this house. [15] “For I was indeed stolen away from the land of the Heḇrews. And also here I have done naught that they should put me into the dungeon.” [16] And when the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Yosĕph, “I also was in my dream, and see, three white baskets were on my head. [17] “And in the uppermost basket were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.” [18] And Yosĕph answered and said, “This is the interpretation of it: The three baskets are three days. [19] “Yet within three days Pharaoh shall lift off your head from you and hang you on a tree. And the birds shall eat your flesh from you.” [20] And it came to be on the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants. And he lifted up the head of the chief butler and the head of the chief baker among his servants. [21] And he restored the chief butler to his post of butler again, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand. [22] But he hanged the chief baker, as Yosĕph had interpreted to them. [23] Yet the chief butler did not remember Yosĕph, but forgot him.

readings.title: The Death of Isaac
readings.text: [Genesis 35:28] And the days of Yitsḥaq were one hundred and eighty years. [29] And Yitsḥaq breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, aged and satisfied of days. And his sons Ěsaw and Ya’aqoḇ buried him.

readings.title: Pharaoh’s Dreams
readings.text: [Genesis 41:1] And it came to be, at the end of two years of days, that Pharaoh dreamed, and see, he was standing by the river. [2] And see, seven cows coming up out of the river, fine looking and fat-fleshed. And they fed in the reed-grass. [3] And see, seven other cows coming up after them out of the river, ugly and lean-fleshed, and stood by the other cows on the bank of the river. [4] And the ugly and lean-fleshed cows ate up the seven fine looking and fat cows. Then Pharaoh awoke. [5] And he slept and dreamed a second time, and see, seven heads of grain coming up on one stalk, plump and good. [6] And see, seven heads, lean and scorched by the east wind, coming up after them. [7] And the seven lean heads swallowed the seven plump and full heads. Then Pharaoh awoke, and see, it was a dream. [8] And it came to be in the morning that his spirit was moved, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Mitsrayim and all its wise men. And Pharaoh related his dreams to them, but there was no one to interpret them to Pharaoh. [9] Then the chief butler spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my sins today. [10] “Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in confinement in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker. [11] “And we dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream. [12] “And there was with us a Heḇrew youth, a servant of the captain of the guard. And we related to him, and he interpreted our dreams for us. He interpreted to each one according to his own dream. [13] “And it came to be, as he interpreted to us, so it came to be. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.” [14] Then Pharaoh sent and called Yosĕph, and they hurriedly brought him out of the dungeon. And he shaved and changed his garments, and came to Pharaoh. [15] And Pharaoh said to Yosĕph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that you understand a dream, to interpret it.” [16] And Yosĕph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It is not in me, <dn>Elohim</dn> shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.” [17] And Pharaoh said to Yosĕph, “In my dream, see, I was standing on the bank of the river. [18] “And see, seven cows coming up out of the river, fat-fleshed and fine looking. And they fed in the reed-grass. [19] “And see, seven other cows coming up after them, poor and very ugly and lean-fleshed, such as I have never seen in all the land of Mitsrayim for ugliness. [20] “And the lean and ugly cows ate up the first seven fat cows. [21] “And when they had eaten them up, no one would have known that they had eaten them, for their appearance was as ugly as at the beginning. Then I awoke. [22] “And I looked in my dream, and see, seven heads of grain coming up on one stalk, full and good. [23] “And see, seven heads, withered, lean, scorched by the east wind, coming up after them. [24] “And the lean heads swallowed the seven good heads. And I spoke to the magicians, but there was no one to explain it to me.” [25] And Yosĕph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown Pharaoh what <dn>He</dn> is about to do: [26] “The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads are seven years – the dream is one. [27] “And the seven lean and ugly cows coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty heads scorched by the east wind are seven years of scarcity. [28] “This is the word which I spoke to Pharaoh. <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown Pharaoh what <dn>He</dn> is about to do. [29] “See, seven years of great plenty are coming throughout all the land of Mitsrayim, [30] “but after them seven years of scarcity shall arise, and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Mitsrayim. And the scarcity shall consume the land, [31] “and the plenty shall not be noticed in the land because of the scarcity following, for it is very severe. [32] “And the dream was repeated to Pharaoh twice because the matter is established by <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> is hastening to do it. [33] “And now, let Pharaoh look for a man discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Mitsrayim. [34] “Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, to take up a fifth of the adjoining land of Mitsrayim in the seven years of plenty. [35] “And let them gather all the food of those good years that are coming, and store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities. [36] “And let the food be as a reserve for the land for the seven years of scarcity which shall be in the land of Mitsrayim, so that the land is not cut off by the scarcity.”

readings.title: Joseph Exalted over Egypt
readings.text: [Genesis 41:37] And the word was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants. [38] And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn>?” [39] And Pharaoh said to Yosĕph, “Since <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown you all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you. [40] “You yourself shall be over my house, and all my people shall be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne am I greater than you.” [41] And Pharaoh said to Yosĕph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Mitsrayim.” [42] And Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand and put it on Yosĕph’s hand, and he dressed him in garments of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck. [43] And he had him ride in the second chariot which he had, and they cried out before him, “Bow the knee!” And he set him over all the land of Mitsrayim. [44] And Pharaoh said to Yosĕph, “I am Pharaoh, and without your word no man shall lift his hand or foot in all the land of Mitsrayim.” [45] And Pharaoh called Yosĕph’s name Tsaphenath-Pa’nĕaḥ. And he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On, as a wife. So Yosĕph went out over all the land of Mitsrayim. [46] And Yosĕph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim. And Yosĕph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Mitsrayim. [47] And in the seven years of plenty the ground brought forth by handfuls. [48] So he gathered all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Mitsrayim, and laid up the food in the cities. He laid up in every city the food of the fields which surrounded them. [49] And Yosĕph gathered very much grain, as the sand of the sea, until he ceased measuring, for it was without number. [50] And to Yosĕph were born two sons before the years of scarcity came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On, bore to him. [51] And Yosĕph called the name of the first-born Menashsheh, “For <dn>Elohim</dn> has made me forget all my toil and all my father’s house.” [52] And the name of the second he called Ephrayim, “For <dn>Elohim</dn> has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.” [53] And the seven years of plenty which were in the land of Mitsrayim came to an end, [54] and the seven years of scarcity began to come, as Yosĕph had said. And the scarcity was in all lands, but in all the land of Mitsrayim there was bread. [55] And when all the land of Mitsrayim was hungry, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all the Mitsrites, “Go to Yosĕph. Do whatever he says to you.” [56] And the scarcity was on all the face of the earth, and Yosĕph opened all the storehouses and sold to the Mitsrites. And the scarcity was severe in the land of Mitsrayim. [57] And all the earth came to Mitsrayim to Yosĕph to buy grain, because the scarcity was severe in all the earth.
